restrictions: Target sha3-256-r5-prefix-v1 exactly: Keccak-f[1600] rounds 0..4 on the single absorbed block, zero IV, rate 1088, SHA3 suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, full 256-bit digest. Both messages are 135 bytes, so the padded block ends in 0x86 and 520 state bits are fixed. The collision is ordinary.
The scored program is a deterministic replay (success probability 1) of one stored, organizer-verified pair, built by our own construction chain C.

C uses no published or third-party colliding pair, connector, subspace or difference beta0/beta1/alpha1. Its only external input is the published trail core No. 3 of GLL+20 Table 9 (beta2, beta3), a difference pattern that is not a collision. C computes its own beta1 order, prefilter, joint CryptoMiniSat witness (committed seed), witness-anchored connector space (DF 58) and its own phase-D enumeration until the first collision.

Total time is the executed work of C plus every diagnostic run after the commitment: phase B (Python and CryptoMiniSat), the instrumented re-execution of phase B and the compilations at 256 word operations per retired instruction; our own phase-D program and the diagnostic scans from an instrumented counting twin (traced data-path operations per event, times 4 for memory traffic; 73615736832 pairs over all 10 threads); plus the replay: 2^37.9475 units. The full source, the commitments and the raw records are in the proof appendices.
Memory is a reported metric only. baseline_improved names the organizer reference and does not assert an improvement over any submitted score.

heuristics.statement: Trail core No. 3 of GLL+20 (Table 9: beta2 and beta3, the text of proof Appendix B.6) is public algorithm text that C may read without charging its original search. It is a differential characteristic, not a collision, and contains no message, state value, connector or pair.
heuristics.scope: The trail text only; every other object (beta1, alpha1, beta0, witness, space, pair) is computed and charged inside C.
heuristics.extrapolation: Reads the cost model's rule on search omitted from the submitted program as covering searches whose outputs are specific to the submitted instance or run; the trail is a published characteristic of the permutation, used by GLL+20 for SHA3-224 and SHA3-256.
heuristics.limitations: If the trail search must be charged, the bound rises by its cost, which GLL+20 do not report and we did not execute. A public package on this track caps its own executed search for this core at 2^38.82 units under its own accounting; adding that would give 2^39.45. Its 850 bytes are counted as advice.

heuristics.statement: For our phase-D program, the traced data-path operations per event of the counting twin r5count.c (606 per enumerated pair, 25 per row test plus 1 per row passed, 2403 per Stage-1 pass, at most 1,538 per chunk), times 4 for two operand loads and one result store per operation, bound its primitive 256-bit word operations; with the executed event counts this is 1.868 units per enumerated pair on average.
heuristics.scope: Phase D as executed (r5search.c, keccak_unrolled.h) and the diagnostic scans; the counting twin runs the same loop on the committed space and reproduces the collision and the pass count.
heuristics.extrapolation: Applies the per-event constants traced on two 2^24-index chunks to every event of the run; the code path per event class is fixed.
heuristics.limitations: Data-path operations are traced; memory accesses are charged by the register-free convention (factor 4), not traced. The twin is a separate build of the same loop.

heuristics.statement: For phase B (Python 3.12 with CryptoMiniSat), its instrumented re-execution, the compilations and the diagnostic scripts, 256 primitive 256-bit word operations per retired AArch64 instruction bound their work.
heuristics.scope: The processes whose retired-instruction counters are in proof Appendix C (phase B 284576788169, re-execution 282494312169, compilation 558963823); the per-phase trace is in proof Section 7.1.
heuristics.extrapolation: Applies a per-instruction emulation bound to every retired instruction of these processes, including library code.
heuristics.limitations: The per-instruction factor is a convention, not verified by an instrumented emulation; instruction counts are the macOS counters on Apple M4 Pro. The instruction-charged lines are 42.0% of the total; a factor 1024 would add 1.18 bits.

heuristics.statement: The charged chain C covers all computation of this construction, from its tables to the stored pair, including every prefilter test, SAT attempt, thread and check. Development runs with other labels and seeds (disclosed in proof Section 12) are not part of C; C reads none of their outputs and recomputes everything from the trail text and its committed seed.
heuristics.scope: Construction chain C as committed in proof Appendix A before its execution.
heuristics.extrapolation: Treats development that fixed only design constants (listed in proof Section 12: the candidate order, the prefilter, the SAT encoding and its bounds, the acceptance threshold, the export and search parameters) as algorithm design rather than as search omitted from the submitted program; the two target-specific facts it revealed are recomputed in C.
heuristics.limitations: The commitment is a local git commit and file timestamp, not an external notarisation. Development work (about 7e12 retired instructions) is disclosed but not charged; charged at 256 per instruction it would give about 2^40.53.

heuristics.statement: Peak memory over C is below 2^29 bytes: the inventory of code files, tables, intermediate files and advice plus the measured phase-B resident set is 262369451 bytes.
heuristics.scope: The inventory of proof Section 10 (mem_inventory.py) and the measured peaks of phases B and D.
heuristics.extrapolation: Counts code by on-disk size of mapped and imported files and adds it to the resident set even where the resident set already contains it.
heuristics.limitations: Resident set size is the operating system's measure, not a RAM-model word count; the beta1-order size is an estimate inside the measured resident set.
